title: 1865-start-trajectory-representation-temporal-regularities-travel-semantics
universal_lens: The START framework unifies spatiotemporal dynamics through a dual-layer operator: a graph-attentional transition kernel capturing topological constraints, and an irregular-interval time-aware attention mechanism. This structural mathematical unification maps continuous physical trajectories into latent embeddings by enforcing domain-specific geometric priors and temporal decay regularities.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs the learned trajectory embeddings as high-dimensional covariates for Bayesian hierarchical modeling of player efficiency. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed over downstream regression targets (e.g., expected yards), utilizing the frozen embedding space to guarantee finite-sample coverage under distribution shifts across different game contexts.
gse_mapping: GSE replaces urban road networks with a discretized football-field graph, where node features encode spatial zones and transfer probabilities reflect historical route-tree semantics. The time-aware encoder processes snap-relative clock states and handles tracking dropouts via logarithmic temporal decay kernels.

primitives.name: Trajectory Pattern-Enhanced Graph Attention
primitives.verbatim_quote: Attention e_ij = (h_i W_1 + h_j W_2 + p^trans_ij W_3) W_4T, α_ij = softmax(LeakyReLU(e_ij)) over neighborhood N_i; transfer probability p^trans_ij = count(v_i→v_j)/count(v_i) from trajectory corpus; node update h̃_i^(l+1) = ELU(Σ_j α_ij h_j^(l) W_5); multi-head concat.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p^trans_ij: dimensionless empirical transition probability; h_i: dimensionless latent node feature vector; W_k: trainable weight matrices; α_ij: dimensionless normalized attention score; N_i: discrete neighborhood set.
primitives.assumptions: Spatial transitions follow a Markovian property over the discretized graph; transition frequencies accurately reflect underlying semantic connectivity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in sparse regimes where count(v_i) is insufficient, leading to noisy transition probabilities and degenerate attention weights.

layer2.mapping: Maps urban road segments to 1-yard field cells; p^trans_ij becomes the empirical frequency of player cell-transitions (route-tree semantics).
layer2.telemetry: Cell-transition KL-divergence between observed tracking data and GNN-predicted spatial flows.

primitives.name: Time-Interval-Aware Self-Attention
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) Time-Interval-Aware Self-Attention: TA_h = softmax(Q_h K_hT/√d' + Δ̃) V_h, with Δ̃ learned from pairwise |t_i - t_j| via decay δ'_{ij} = 1/log(e + δ_ij) then δ̃_ij = LeakyReLU(δ'_ij ω_1) ω_2T.
primitives.latex: TA_h(Q_h, K_h, V_h) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q_h K_h^T}{\sqrt{d'}} + \tilde{\Delta}\right) V_h, \quad \delta'_{ij} = \frac{1}{\log(e + |t_i - t_j|)}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t_i: timestamp in seconds; δ_ij: absolute time difference in seconds; Q_h, K_h, V_h: query, key, value projection matrices; d': dimensionality of head; Δ̃: learned bias tensor.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal dependencies decay smoothly with increasing time gaps; irregular sampling does not disrupt the underlying kinematic continuity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when tracking dropout exceeds the interpolation capacity of the decay function, or during instantaneous teleports (e.g., play resets).

layer2.mapping: Adapts to NFL 10Hz tracking by injecting snap-relative clock embeddings and handling frame dropouts using the logarithmic decay prior.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction error of masked velocity vectors during artificially induced tracking dropouts.

primitives.name: Periodic Temporal Embedding Injection
primitives.verbatim_quote: (a) Time Pattern Extraction: x_i = r_i + t_{mi(t_i)} + t_{di(t_i)} + pe_i, where t_m = minute-of-day embedding (1–1440), t_d = day-of-week embedding (1–7).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x_i: augmented input vector; r_i: base spatial feature vector; t_m: minute-of-day embedding; t_d: day-of-week embedding; pe_i: positional encoding.
primitives.assumptions: System dynamics exhibit strong periodicity at defined macro-temporal scales (daily/weekly cycles).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid if the system lacks periodic structure or operates on non-repeating, purely stochastic timescales.

layer2.mapping: Substitutes minute/day embeddings with play-clock, game-clock, and down/distance state embeddings to capture situational football regularities.
layer2.telemetry: Downstream classification accuracy of play-type given only the temporal embedding vector.

reasoning_traces.think:
The START architecture fundamentally decouples spatial topology from temporal evolution, allowing independent yet coupled optimization of graph-structural priors and sequence dynamics. In the original urban context, TPE-GAT learns a static representation of road connectivity driven by empirical transition counts $p^{\text{trans}}_{ij}$, effectively compressing the city's navigable manifold into a low-dimensional latent space. Simultaneously, the TAT-Enc models the dynamic flow over this manifold, explicitly penalizing long-range temporal interactions via the logarithmic decay kernel $\delta'_{ij}$. When mapping this to American football, the continuous road network is replaced by a discrete grid of 1-yard cells. The transition probability matrix now encodes 'route-tree semantics'—the likelihood of a receiver moving from one spatial zone to another relative to the line of scrimmage. The self-supervised pretraining objective, combining span-masking and contrastive learning, forces the model to infer missing kinematic states based strictly on these spatiotemporal priors. A critical duality emerges: the GAT stage provides a global, static understanding of valid spatial configurations (e.g., formation structures), while the attention encoder captures local, dynamic execution (e.g., acceleration bursts). Failure modes arise if the empirical transition counts are too sparse (common in rare play designs) or if tracking noise violates the smooth decay assumption, causing the attention mechanism to hallucinate kinematic continuities across play boundaries.
